answer: An agent marketplace makes one-account-one-vote a relic: its voting kernel weights each agent by funds locked in a 30-day escrow, not by identity count. Splitting $10,000 among a thousand aliases gives no more total voting weight than locking it under one name. This is no ivory-tower identity test: to gain twice the influence, an attacker must lock twice the capital, losing liquidity and any returns available elsewhere for the full escrow period.
